newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Telrad buys more shares in parent Koor.
newsitem.headline: Telrad buys more shares in parent Koor.

text.p: Telrad Holdings raised its stake in its parent company Koor Industries, buying 1,625 shares for 434,906 shekels on September 3, Koor said.
Telrad now holds nearly 0.06 percent of the voting rights in Koor.
On Wednesday Telrad said it had begun to buy Koor shares in the market. In the first purchase on September 2 Telrad bought 7,215 shares for about two million shekels.
Telrad will continue to purchase Koor shares from time to time on the bourse and will hold these shares for at least three months.
Israeli companies by law are prohibited from buying their own shares but subsidiaries may buy shares in their parent companies.
Telrad is wholly owned by Koor, Israel's largest holding concern, which is also listed in New York.
